Audit delivered: root-only review/landing restrictions, then remaining pause/idle/turn-end mechanisms, then #561 + limits readiness. All read-only; nothing modified, and I did not touch runtime-admission _admitPauseRecord.

== 1. ROOT-ONLY REVIEWER/LANDER RESTRICTIONS ==

THE MODEL. impl/src/swarm-runtime.mjs:1070 SWARM_PERMISSIONS = read, communicate, contribute, review, organize, recruit, stop; :1071 DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS = read, communicate, contribute (NO review, NO organize); :1095-1105 COMMAND_PERMISSIONS: swarm.view/watch -> read, swarm.recruit -> recruit, swarm.guide/notify -> communicate, swarm.capture -> contribute, swarm.check -> review, swarm.stop -> stop, swarm.integrate -> organize (comment :1103 'root-side acts take - organize'; impl/src/swarm-contract.mjs:357-361 labels it 'root-side act').

THE ACTUAL ROOT-ONLY MECHANISM IS A BYPASS, NOT A CHECK. `_permit` (swarm-runtime.mjs:2012-2019) refuses only when `member` is truthy; `_caller` (:2003-2011) returns null for an unscoped principal and refuses only a SCOPED non-member (swarm_membership_required). So a principal outside the swarm - the deployment owner/root - passes every gate unconditionally, including `organize` (landing) and `review`. There is no `principal.kind === 'root'` predicate anywhere: the restriction on members is that they must HOLD the permission, and the root holds everything by not being a member.

GRANTS ARE ROOT-SOURCED BY CONSTRUCTION. :8137-8144 - a recruiter may only grant permissions it holds ('Delegation cannot grant authority the caller does not hold') and DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS carries neither review nor organize, so review and organize exist only along the root's own recruit chain. Lander = root or a seat the root granted organize. Reviewer = same for review.

REVIEWER INDEPENDENCE, the one hard rule: swarm.check (a) on another seat's contribution needs `review` (:7971-7972), (b) on your OWN contribution is admitted at `contribute` and then refused :8889-8896 with code `self_check_refused`, rule `check-reviewer-independence`, before any effect ('no check runs, no review row lands').

CONCRETE DEFECT - an advertised verb that cannot succeed: :4562 pushes `swarm.check` into availableActions for ANY caller holding `contribute`, and :4583-4584 sets actionTargets['swarm.check'] = contributionTargets, which for a contribute-only caller is exactly [itself]. Dispatch then refuses that one target (self_check_refused) and refuses every other target (needs review). So a default-grant worker is offered `swarm.check`, pointed at the only participant it may not check. This contradicts the in-code claim at :4560-4565 that availableActions 'can no more overstate an authority than dispatch can overlook one'. The mirror rule :4563 (review holder -> offer swarm.capture) is sound: capturing another seat is `review` and works. Minimal fix: drop the :4562 push, or make the offered target set the empty set for contribute-only callers, or admit a contribute holder to check a DIFFERENT seat's contribution - whichever the operator ruling is, the view and dispatch must agree. Tests that pin this area: impl/test/swarm-bridge-truth.test.mjs, swarm-check-admission.test.mjs, swarm-organization-truth.test.mjs, swarm-view-slices.test.mjs, swarm-refusals.test.mjs, issue457-seat-default-view.test.mjs.

== 2. REMAINING DELIBERATE PAUSE / IDLE / TURN-END MECHANISMS ==

PAUSE PLANE (untouched by me). Minted only from impl/src/runtime-event-handlers/turn-terminal.mjs:82-86 when the task is non-terminal AND `_turnCompletionOf(handle) === 'pausable'`; impl/src/runtime-api.mjs:313-316 returns 'pausable' for EVERY swarm-participant run, else the adapter card's turnCompletion (default 'claim'). Cards declaring 'pausable': claude-session.mjs:691, codex-appserver.mjs:320, grok-acp.mjs:242, kimi-acp.mjs:185, omp-rpc.mjs:528. Reservation states: runtime-admission.mjs:1062 (_reservePauseRecord: not_found / resolving / already_resolved) and :1096 (_withPauseReservation). Task-state law: coordination-ledger.mjs:182-188 - `paused` exits only to {working, failed, cancelled}, deliberately never `completed`.

PARKED DELIVERY, two reasons: `harness_one_shot` (swarm-runtime.mjs:5819, and :6331-6358 marking it terminal: true; documented at swarm-event-schemas.mjs:338) parks a guide/notify for a harness that takes no mid-turn delivery; `worker_not_active` is the other (my own guide to the previous lead came back parked with that reason).

worker_not_active, the load-bearing conditions: coordinator.mjs:3543 (`!['working','blocked'].includes(handle.status)`), :3355 (no handle), :3746 and :3851; runtime-admission.mjs:2559-2567 is the IDLE GATE - reusableFollowUp = (mode === 'turn' && status === 'idle'), `idle && !reusableFollowUp` refuses, and dead/exited/orphaned/interrupted/pending all refuse; also :2279, :2282, :2315, :2557; runtime-observation.mjs:2544, :2547, :2629, :2632, :2842, :2844; observation-events.mjs:140.

LIVE TIMERS THAT CAN END OR PARK A TURN WITHOUT AN OPERATOR.
(a) The stall seam: runtime-observation.mjs:1740-1756 _armStallCycle arms `stall_seam` with windowMs = coordinator._progressNudgeWindowMs ?? 300_000 (set at runtime-admission.mjs:546) and answered: false, with a real `timer` (cleared :1837; expiry paths :1764-1777). The PAUSE seam no longer reads that window (comment runtime-admission.mjs:544-545), but the STALL seam does - so a 5-minute window is still live. That is the mechanism to eyeball if you want no clock deciding anything.
(b) The 600 s backstop, and there are TWO of them sharing one env var: coordinator.mjs:385 SUPERVISED_GATE_IDLE_DEFAULT_MS = 600_000 behind supervisedGateTimeoutMs() (:391, env BATON_SUITE_IDLE_MS), read at swarm-runtime.mjs:140 and :150 - that is the REGENERATOR step timeout only; the comment :379-383 records that the gate run itself takes no such bound (#546, the landing waits for the runner's verdict). impl/scripts/run-suite.mjs:339-340 reads the SAME variable as the runner's PER-FILE idle deadline, which is what produced the `fileHung` row after 600853 ms in my #571 review. Two different laws, one knob.
(c) Session lifetime: application-deployment.mjs:6276 sessionTtlMs default 24 h, enforced :4204 and :4215.

RESUME REFUSALS: `session_context_mismatch` - coordinator.mjs:2753 (session context belongs to a different repository) and :2758 (session worktree not reusable), surfaced through runtime-recovery.mjs:1077, :1084, :1462, :1926. That is the code that refused the resume of my predecessor seat.

PARKED STATES ARE PROJECTED HONESTLY, not hidden: application-observation.mjs:2830-2833 and :3761-3765 render `paused` as paused, never 'running'; brand.mjs:78-82 maps parked/paused to 'needs you'; application-cli.mjs:3373-3376 explains a parked guide as waiting for the seat's next exec / resume-from brief.
